title: TOPIC-DIFFICULTY: does a difficulty axis inside a cell change the judge and the model order? (zero judge calls)
question: Inside a cell (the 14 bareq512_s42 anchors) the questions span the whole difficulty range (roster accuracy on the key, quartiles 0.283 / 0.500 / 0.739). Does the judge behave differently on the easy and hard terciles of the SAME cell (verification fidelity, tie rate, length preference), and is the within-cell model order on hard questions the order on easy ones? Claim under test: per-cell boards are NOT difficulty-invariant.

sentence_of_record: TOPIC-DIFFICULTY (zero calls; MISTRAL-MERGED, 21,536 verdicts, 2,811 judged questions, terciles within the 14 bareq512_s42 anchors by 46-model key accuracy): key-decidable accuracy A falls 15.5pp [-18.5, -12.4] and the key-decidable tie rate rises 6.6pp [+5.0, +8.3] from the easy to the hard tercile (same sign on x12, grok, Kotlin), but 72-79% of the accuracy drop is the reference's (reference-correct rate 98.4% -> 77.7%; within reference-correct the judge's own drop is -4.5pp [-6.7, -2.5]): REF-BY-CELL inside a cell, not a new judge effect. The registered length contrast on all decisive matches reads easy +1.525 > hard +0.556/1k (z -12.9) and is a composition artefact (66% of easy matches are both-right pairs on which the judge takes the longer answer at +3.4/1k); on key-decidable matches it is easy +0.145 vs hard +0.294 (z +1.9; x12 +1.6, grok -0.5, Kotlin 0.0): C3 FAILED on the registered statistic, UNDETERMINED on the verification-relevant one. The easy-vs-hard order is below the within-cell permutation null in 4-5 of 14 anchors (seed-dependent at Economics), median rho 0.898; C4 FAILED; the key's 0.809 is ceiling-compressed and not a capability benchmark. C5 is a count, not a finding: 1 of 31 vs 5 of 32 wrong-direction (Fisher p 0.20, [-0.7, +27.3]pp; convention A 6.5% vs 31.3% carried by 5 ties), hard stratum 3 pairs: UNDETERMINED. Every stratum board is UNDETERMINED (nominal < 3; 11 established wrong of 5,233 called), so a difficulty-stratified reading certifies nothing the whole-cell board does not; the key-free plurality proxy (Spearman 0.785, tercile agreement 0.745) recovers -6.8pp [-9.5, -4.0] of the contrast and has no edge-level test; its use in the widener needs its own registration.

plain_description.what: Re-reads about 21,500 existing verdicts (no new calls), splitting each cell's questions into easy, middle and hard thirds, and compares judge accuracy, ties, length preference and model order between easy and hard.
plain_description.why: Tests whether a single per-cell ranking is misleading because the judge behaves differently on hard questions within the same cell.
plain_description.information: A difference would require difficulty-split rankings. Result: done; judge accuracy drops 15.5 points on hard questions, but 72-79% of that is because the reference answer is more often wrong there, not a new judge effect; no reliable length or model-order difference; every difficulty-split ranking is undetermined. On the older p2dca question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
